title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: The overwhelming trader consensus against a US default by the end of 2027 stems from repeated congressional action to raise or suspend the debt ceiling, Treasury use of extraordinary measures, and bipartisan recognition that crossing the threshold would trigger severe market disruptions and higher borrowing costs. With the current statutory limit extended through prior legislation and no acute fiscal cliff scheduled before late 2026 or 2027, markets price the risk as remote. Historical precedent shows Congress resolving limit impasses at the last moment, while strong US economic fundamentals and global demand for Treasuries reinforce the view that outright default is avoidable. Remaining tail risks include an unprecedented failure of debt-ceiling negotiations amid extreme polarization or a sudden fiscal shock, though both remain low-probability events within the resolution window.
